title: Create the dedicated Newsense implementation repo and planning scaffold
summary: Create the private GitHub repo, seed the planning artifacts, and establish the basic folder structure for the website codebase.
acceptance: The repo `sheshiyer/newsense` exists and is reachable.
The repo contains the planning note and backlog seed.
The repo documents the vault as the canonical upstream content source.

title: Normalize the extracted Newsense archive into a build-ready content package
summary: Convert the legacy scrape outputs into normalized studio, client, project, archive, and media data files that the new site can consume directly.
acceptance: All recovered studio, team, services, contact, and project data are represented in the new repo.
Placeholder routes are marked as archive items instead of featured projects.
Media references resolve to local asset paths or explicit provenance warnings.

title: Define Newsense brand guardrails and asset governance for the rebuild
summary: Lock the studio-first brand rules, preserve the wordmark usage, and define which imagery belongs to studio identity vs client case-study contexts.
acceptance: The preserved wordmark is documented as the canonical logo lockup.
Studio identity references are separated from client-case imagery.
Owned and generated asset usage rules are explicit for future scene work.

title: Freeze the information architecture, object map, and case-study taxonomy
summary: Convert the Newsense content model into a stable website information architecture with named views, object mappings, and case-study types.
acceptance: Top-level navigation objects and their corresponding views are finalized.
Projects are classified into the agreed case-study types.
Archive handling and fallback information paths are documented.

title: Fork False Earth into a reduced Newsense scene shell
summary: Use `false-earth` as the starting codebase, strip the astronaut/gameplay-specific systems, and preserve only the scene infrastructure that makes sense for Newsense.
acceptance: The repo runs as a clean Newsense shell rather than the original game-like demo.
Unused traversal, terrain, and world narrative code are removed or isolated.
The shell still builds and preserves a coherent loading/render pipeline.

title: Implement capability detection and fallback delivery modes
summary: Add explicit runtime handling for immersive WebGPU, reduced 3D, and editorial fallback modes so the site remains usable on non-WebGPU devices.
acceptance: WebGPU support is detected before immersive features are enabled.
A reduced or fallback mode exists for unsupported browsers/devices.
Core Newsense content remains accessible across all delivery modes.

title: Build the object-selection, camera choreography, and scene-state system
summary: Replace free traversal with deliberate object-based navigation, camera framing, hover/focus states, and view transitions.
acceptance: Each top-level object can be focused and opened intentionally.
Camera movement reinforces hierarchy instead of behaving like gameplay controls.
The selected object state drives the content overlay/view system.

title: Implement loading, audio, quality, and accessibility controls for the scene shell
summary: Turn the current scene controls into a website-appropriate system that handles loading, reduced motion, quality modes, and optional audio without relying on game metaphors.
acceptance: Loading and quality controls are understandable in a studio-site context.
Reduced-motion and mute-first behaviors are supported.
The controls degrade cleanly across fallback modes.

title: Build the Newsense stage view and homepage object experience
summary: Create the landing state around the preserved wordmark, studio positioning, and a restrained first interaction that opens the wider object system.
acceptance: The stage view feels like Newsense rather than a generic scene wrapper.
The wordmark is preserved and used as the main orientation anchor.
The first interaction leads cleanly into the project/studio objects.

title: Build the project atlas object and work discovery system
summary: Create the primary work-discovery object with grouped previews, category filters, and selection states that can bridge into detailed case-study views.
acceptance: Projects can be browsed by meaningful groupings rather than a flat list.
The atlas supports movement or transitions without losing orientation.
Selecting a project opens the correct case-study route or overlay.

title: Implement the motion-first case-study template
summary: Build the template for video-heavy product and launch projects with strong motion/media treatment, credits, and concise supporting text.
acceptance: Motion-led projects can be presented without feeling like pasted portfolio pages.
Local video assets, stills, and credits all render cleanly.
The template remains performant on both immersive and reduced modes.

title: Implement the campaign/system case-study template
summary: Build the narrative-first template for projects with process steps, identity work, collateral, and outcomes.
acceptance: Narrative sections and process steps have a clear visual hierarchy.
Collateral and identity assets can be shown without turning into a generic image dump.
The template can handle long-form projects like `re-outland` and `oneplus-softgold`.

title: Implement the editorial, stills, and archive case-study template
summary: Build the template for photography-led work and the lower-emphasis archive presentation used for preserved placeholder routes.
acceptance: Photography-led work gets its own calmer presentation rhythm.
Archive items are preserved but clearly separated from live featured work.
Provenance warnings can be surfaced where the source archive is ambiguous.

title: Import all preserved Newsense projects into the new presentation system
summary: Map every recovered project into its final case-study type, populate its content, and confirm the archive split between flagship and placeholder work.
acceptance: All recovered projects exist in the new registry.
Featured vs archive routing matches the agreed taxonomy.
Known source warnings are preserved where they affect presentation trust.

title: Build the studio, about, and services surface
summary: Create the Newsense studio view with positioning, manifesto, services, and method presented as a deliberate spatial/editorial surface rather than a static About page.
acceptance: The studio surface preserves the recovered About content without flattening it.
Services and positioning feel integrated into the site system.
The view reads as studio identity, not client work.

title: Build the team and client-proof surface
summary: Present the core team, client roster, and credits/proof in a way that supports trust without becoming a generic agency grid.
acceptance: Amyth, Sant, and Suraj each have a clear presentation with preserved bios.
Client proof is visible but does not overpower the work.
Credits and role language stay faithful to the archive.

title: Build the contact and inquiry surface
summary: Create the contact object and view with email, phone, location, and a strong call to collaborate that works in immersive and fallback modes.
acceptance: All preserved contact details are available and easy to reach.
The contact path remains obvious from every mode.
The CTA language matches the refined Newsense brand tone.

title: Generate and curate owned Newsense visual assets for the scene objects
summary: Create or curate owned atmospheric visuals, materials, and stills that support the scene objects without relying on mixed client-collage references.
acceptance: Scene objects have Newsense-owned visual material to work with.
Studio identity assets are kept separate from client-case imagery.
The asset set supports both homepage atmosphere and section transitions.

title: Curate the final transition and interaction language from compatible Codrops patterns
summary: Select and integrate the strongest interaction ideas from the shortlisted references so the whole site feels cohesive rather than like multiple demos stitched together.
acceptance: Transitions feel like one language across homepage, atlas, and case studies.
The final motion system supports the Newsense tone instead of demo novelty.
Interaction choices are documented against the Codrops shortlist.

title: Run QA, ship the first deployment, and prepare editorial handoff
summary: Verify accessibility, performance, browser/device behavior, content fidelity, and deployment readiness, then prepare the repo for ongoing editorial updates.
acceptance: The site passes the agreed QA matrix across immersive and fallback modes.
Deployment instructions and environment assumptions are documented.
Editorial/content update workflows are clear for future iteration.
